entities.summary: Cipus was a public servant of the Classical era, active in the late 5th century BCE, who played a crucial role in the governance of the city-state of Athens. As a military commander, he led Athenian forces in the Peloponnesian War, contributing significantly to the city's defeat and the rise of Thebes. Cipus's legacy extends to the development of Athenian democracy, as his reforms aimed to increase citizen participation and reduce aristocratic influence. His influence can also be seen in the subsequent rise of Alexander the Great, who built upon the foundations laid by Cipus and expanded Athenian power throughout the Mediterranean. Through his contributions to Athenian governance and warfare, Cipus left a lasting impact on the development of Western civilization. This impact can be seen in the enduring legacy of the Athenian democracy, which continues to shape modern political systems. Cipus's story serves as a testament to the enduring power of human ingenuity and the importance of civic engagement in shaping the course of history.
